annotations.text:
CAPTURE
Every capture starts with a command. Row 1 is discovery and the moment of capture. Row 2 is the three ways it does not go cleanly: a question left waiting, text typed without a command, and the shared model limit.
Only four commands exist in epic 001, because tasks are the only record type. The filter artboard shows /add matching one command, not six. The palette is built to group as the list grows.
FR-36 to FR-38. The question sits in the transcript and never blocks. /tasks ran underneath it and worked. Nothing is saved until the question is answered, and the answer binds to its own capture.

RECORDS
One type filter, All and Tasks, because tasks are the only record type in this epic. Detail shows the origin and what you actually typed, so a record can always be traced back to the command that made it.
Timezone is the only setting in this epic. Jarvis has one account per user, so the no-permission state can only mean a session that ended.

Two directions not taken, kept low-fi so they read as alternatives rather than half-finished screens. The built direction is warm paper, IBM Plex, one blue for action and one amber for commands. Say the word if either of these is closer.

MOBILE
Same product, same commands, 390x844. The rail becomes a bottom bar, the records table becomes stacked rows, and the three-up field card stacks.

No fake status bar and no fake keyboard are drawn. On MobileCommands the empty band under the input is exactly where the real keyboard renders.
Every control is at least 44px tall. The command list is tap-first here rather than arrow-key first, so the highlighted row is a default rather than a cursor.

INSTALLED APP
Three surfaces a plain web app does not have: the invitation to install, being offline, and a new version waiting.

Offline reads but does not capture. Capture needs a model call, so the input says so plainly instead of queueing work it cannot finish. That keeps the PRD's out-of-scope line on offline capture intact.

No push notification design here on purpose. The approved decision is in-app and email, no push. Installing makes web push cheap to add, which is worth reopening at epic 002 with reminders, as a decision rather than a side effect.

DARK THEME
Not the light palette inverted. Warm near-black rather than blue-grey, because the light theme is warm paper and both have to read as one product. Accents lighten so they stay legible; the token sheet gives every pair.

The theme follows the operating system, with an override in settings. That override is a setting the PRD does not currently have.

NAME AND LOGO
Four candidates, each with the mark, the app icon, and the identity applied in the product. Every one carries an honest case and an honest cost, because a set where only the favourite gets defended is a rigged vote.

My pick is Magpie. It is the only one here that is both easy to own and a description of what the product does.

Read the Jarvis card before deciding: Jasper.ai shipped as Jarvis.ai and renamed in 2022 after a Marvel trademark dispute. That is not legal advice, it is a reason to spend twenty minutes with someone who gives it.
